author: Adam Savage’s Tested
description:
Adam Savage visits the chemical imaging lab at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C., to explore the cutting-edge science behind art conservation! Teaming up with conservator Joanna Dunn and scientists John Delaney, Kate Dooley and Teresa Duncan, Adam gets an inside look at how hyperspectral imaging, X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) uncover hidden details beneath the surface of an 800-year-old masterpiece painted in egg tempera. From concealed marbleized floor patterns and gilded silver backgrounds to microscopic cross-sections of ancient pigment layers, discover how space-grade technology helps reverse-engineer master artists' techniques and protect cultural heritage.

National Gallery of Art: https://www.nga.gov/
Visit the NGA: https://www.nga.gov/visit
More about Madonna and Child Enthroned With Four Saints: https://www.nga.gov/artworks/41622-madonna-and-child-enthroned-four-saints
